edge.title: World On Edge Index

trend.label: Rising — deadline expired, ties March record

rows.note: US–Iran war · Hormuz closed · index record
Current — Day 171 · deadline expired · ties record

levels.label: Very High — systemic risk indicators active

edge.body: The World On Edge Index rises to 89/100 — tying its March record. The Islamabad Memorandum's 60-day window expired August 17 with no deal: talks deadlocked over Hormuz management and frozen Iranian funds, and Washington now says there is 'no time schedule' for ending the war. Day 171. Since June: the July 8 ceasefire collapse brought 11+ consecutive nights of US strikes reaching Tehran's outskirts, and the Strait of Hormuz went from recovering to effectively shut — zero transits on August 16 against a pre-war ~178/day, with war-risk premiums at 3–10% of hull value. Brent holds near $91, kept below the February $138 peak by reserve releases and demand fears rather than peace. The one live off-ramp: the Iran–Oman shipping-route agreement of August 5, reaffirmed by Tehran even as the deadline lapsed, with Kushner shuttling between Hamas and Netanyahu the same weekend. Beyond the Gulf: Russia's summer offensive grinds at Kupiansk amid US interceptor shortages, and Ethiopia–Tigray clashes near Sheraro are the first since the 2022 Pretoria accord.
edge.method: Five inputs normalized 0–100, weighted and summed. GPR (35%): Caldara & Iacoviello index vs 0–200 range. ACLED (25%): active conflict zones vs 0–80 range. Gallup (15%): worry index as published. Conflict Deaths (15%): YTD deaths vs 50,000 threshold. Species Threat (10%): threatened % vs 50% threshold. Weights at anthonycharts.com/composites-v1.0.json
edge.share: World On Edge: 89/100 — ties the March record. US–Iran war Day 171: the 60-day deal expired with no agreement, Hormuz near zero transits, Brent ~$91. Calm Window 18%. anthonycharts.com 🌍

good.title: World Goodness Index

trend.label: Holding — science and diplomacy offset humanitarian strain

rows.note: Current — strained aid offset by science wins

good.body: The World Goodness Index holds at 47/100. The strain is real: the DRC is fighting the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded — 2,325 deaths across five provinces as of mid-August — Venezuela is digging out from twin June earthquakes that killed 6,400+, and the aid system is absorbing both on top of three wars. But the offsetting column is unusually strong. Artemis II carried four astronauts around the Moon in April — the farthest humans have ever flown. The Roman Space Telescope is fueled for an August 30 launch, nine months early. A Moderna Ebola vaccine entered clinical trials, and Uganda declared its own outbreak over. The July 30 Hamas disarmament roadmap — however contested its implementation — is the first actionable framework of its kind. Quieter wins: an Iran–Oman shipping accord, a Dominican Republic–Venezuela normalization framework, and an Egypt–Sudan dam-rehabilitation agreement.
good.method: Six inputs normalized 0–100, weighted and summed. Aid (20%): OCHA commitments vs 30B USD. Poverty (20%): World Bank rate inverted. Breakthroughs (15%): OWID annual count vs 50. Treaties (15%): UN quarterly signatures vs 30. Social Mobility (15%): World Bank GSMI 0–100. Conservation (15%): % of 30x30 target achieved. Weights at anthonycharts.com/composites-v1.0.json
good.share: World Goodness holds at 47/100 — a record Ebola outbreak and quake recovery strain the aid system, offset by Artemis II, an Ebola vaccine trial, and a Hamas disarmament roadmap. anthonycharts.com 💚

temp.title: Global Temp Anomaly

trend.label: Rising — July tied the hottest month ever recorded

rows.note: July ties July 2024 as hottest month recorded

levels.label: Paris Agreement threshold — first sustained breach projected 2030–35

temp.body: We are 1.45°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial average (12-month trailing, Copernicus ERA5 through July 2026). July 2026 tied July 2024 as the joint-hottest month ever recorded — NOAA scored it joint-warmest of any month, NASA rated it the hottest July — with record July sea-surface temperatures. A strong El Niño is building fast: forecasters give >90% odds of a very strong event this winter, potentially the strongest since 1950, which would push 2027 toward new records. The ten warmest Julys have all come since 2016. 2024 remains the record calendar year at +1.62°C — the first above 1.5°C.
temp.method: 12-month trailing average of global surface temperature anomaly above 1850–1900 pre-industrial mean. Primary: Copernicus C3S ERA5 reanalysis. Cross-referenced with NOAA GISSTEMP and Berkeley Earth. Arc = position in 0–2°C Paris risk corridor. Updated monthly.
temp.share: Global temp: +1.45°C above pre-industrial (12-mo avg). July 2026 tied the hottest month ever recorded — and a super El Niño is building. anthonycharts.com 🌡️

sea.title: Sea Level Rise

trend.label: Rising and accelerating — rate more than doubled since 1993

levels.label: High-risk — major coastal infrastructure at risk

sea.body: Global mean sea level is up ~102mm since 1993 (NASA satellite altimetry), rising at ~4.4mm per year — more than double the early-1990s rate of 2.1mm. A correction this issue: the previous headline of +112mm is not corroborated by NASA's published series (~102mm); the dashboard now tracks NASA's number directly. The acceleration itself is not in dispute — the rate has roughly doubled in three decades, driven by Greenland melt and thermal expansion, and the 2100 high-emission projections still run to +600mm and beyond.
sea.method: Continuous satellite altimetry: TOPEX/Poseidon (1993) → Jason-1/2/3 → Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich (2020–present). Monthly global mean averages from NASA JPL Physical Oceanography DAAC. Arc = position in 0–200mm scale. Rate acceleration from linear trend analysis of 5-year segments.
sea.share: Sea level: +102mm since 1993 (NASA), rising 4.4mm/yr — more than double the 1990s rate. Re-baselined this issue to NASA's published series. anthonycharts.com 🌊

arctic.title: Arctic Sea Ice Extent

trend.label: Well below average — record-low winter max, 9th-lowest August

rows.note: Lowest March extent on record — C3S

levels.label: Climatological baseline for this calendar date

arctic.body: August 2 extent: 7.02M km² — ninth-lowest for the date in the satellite record and 1.38M km² below the 1981–2010 average, with the Kara Sea exceptionally low (UK Met Office August briefing). July averaged 8.29M km², joint-fifth lowest. The March 2026 winter maximum of 14.29M km² statistically tied 2025 for the record low (NASA/NSIDC). The September minimum is highly uncertain but not projected to break 2012's 3.39M km² record. A data note: NSIDC's monthly analyses are suspended after 2025 funding cuts and an AMSR2 sensor outage, so this issue leans on the Met Office briefing — a reminder that the observing system itself is under strain.
arctic.method: NSIDC Sea Ice Index via satellite passive microwave (SMMR, SSM/I, SSMIS). Extent = total ocean area with at least 15% ice concentration. Updated daily. Compared against 1981–2010 median for the same calendar day to remove seasonal signal. Arc = percentile within seasonal historical range.
arctic.share: Arctic ice: 7.02M km² — 9th-lowest for the date, 1.38M below average. The winter maximum tied the record low. anthonycharts.com ❄️

co2.title: CO₂ Concentration

trend.label: Rising — seasonal dip, growth rate re-accelerating

rows.note: +2.1 y/y — seasonal dip, El Niño building

levels.label: Safe zone upper bound — Hansen, 1988 (now exceeded)
High-risk — 2°C warming likely at sustained levels

co2.body: CO₂ at 427.6 ppm (week of August 9, NOAA Mauna Loa) — 53% above pre-industrial. The drop from June's 431 is the Northern Hemisphere growing season breathing in, not progress: year-over-year growth is back up to +2.1 ppm from the La Niña-damped +1.5 earlier this year, and the strengthening El Niño is expected to push the increment higher into 2027. The Keeling Curve's long-run climb remains the fastest in the 800,000-year ice-core record.
co2.method: Continuous measurement at NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory since 1958 (the Keeling Curve). Weekly averages from NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory. Cross-referenced with Scripps Institution CO₂ program. Arc = position between 280ppm (pre-industrial) and 500ppm (extreme risk ceiling).
co2.share: CO₂: 427.6 ppm — that's the seasonal dip, not progress. Growth is back up to +2.1 ppm/yr as El Niño builds. anthonycharts.com 🌿

planet.title: Exoplanet Discovery

trend.label: Rising — JWST accelerating discovery and atmosphere analysis

levels.label: Current count — confirmed via peer review (Feb 2026)
No confirmed biosignatures yet — JWST now capable of detection

planet.body: 6,336 confirmed planets orbiting other stars — 208 added since June, a number that was zero 34 years ago. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is fueled and integrated on its Falcon Heavy, set for August 30 — nine months ahead of schedule — and projected to discover 100,000 more. JWST meanwhile delivered one of the year's biggest results: a 'black hole star' 660 million years after the Big Bang that may explain the mysterious Little Red Dots. And Artemis II's April crewed lunar flyby took humans farther from Earth than they have ever been.
planet.method: Raw count from NASA Exoplanet Archive. Confirmed status requires: peer-reviewed publication, independent verification via secondary detection method, and archive acceptance. Habitable zone defined by orbital distance allowing liquid surface water. Arc = pace toward 10,000 milestone by 2030.
planet.share: 6,336 confirmed exoplanets — and the Roman Telescope launches Aug 30, projected to find 100,000 more. anthonycharts.com 🪐

alien.title: Technosignature Watch

trend.label: No confirmed detection — 'active candidates' metric retired

levels.label: Current — no confirmed extraterrestrial signal ever
Passes RFI filter + multi-beam — still unresolved

alien.body: This issue retires the 'active candidates' count. No observatory or survey publishes such a register, and the FAST candidates previously carried here have no verifiable published status — so the honest headline is the number that has never changed: zero confirmed technosignatures, ever. The searching itself accelerated in 2026: a VLA + MeerKAT narrowband search of K2-18 b returned a null result, Breakthrough Listen's BLUSE commensal survey has autonomously processed 1.2M+ MeerKAT pointings, and a SETI Institute–NVIDIA system now scans the Allen Telescope Array roughly 600× faster. The Wow! Signal turns 49 this week — still unexplained, still never repeated.
alien.method: Confirmed detections from peer-reviewed publications — none exist. The prior 'active candidates' count (FAST 2022 reports) was retired in August 2026: no source publishes an ongoing candidate register, so the dashboard no longer displays one. Survey progress tracked from Breakthrough Listen and SETI Institute publications.
alien.share: Technosignatures confirmed ever: 0. The search got faster in 2026 — 1.2M+ MeerKAT pointings, K2-18 b came up null. Still listening. anthonycharts.com 👽

solar.title: Solar Activity

trend.label: Declining — past Solar Cycle 25 maximum, activity trending lower

levels.label: Current — weak grid fluctuations at high latitudes
Power grid fluctuations, satellite drag increases
Grid collapse risk, widespread satellite damage

solar.body: Solar Cycle 25 remains in its declining phase past the late-2025 peak. NOAA SWPC has a G1 (Minor) watch for August 19, driven by a negative-polarity coronal-hole high-speed stream — the workhorse of a descending cycle — with minor R1–R2 radio blackouts at 35% daily odds. G1 is the mildest storm classification: aurora at high latitudes, negligible infrastructure risk. An earlier G1 storm passed on August 3 without incident.
solar.method: 24-hour peak geomagnetic storm rating from NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC). G-scale from Kp-index: G1=Kp≥5, G2=Kp≥6, G3=Kp≥7, G4=Kp≥8, G5=Kp=9. Sunspot number from WDC-SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium — international standard since 1849.
solar.share: Solar Activity: G1 watch for Aug 19. Cycle 25 descending — coronal-hole streams drive the weather now. anthonycharts.com ☀️

neo.title: Near-Earth Object Watch

trend.label: Catalog growing — more known = safer, not more dangerous

levels.label: Current — no objects on impact trajectory
Within 0.05 AU (~7.5M km) — tracked, not threatening
>140m diameter + passes within 0.05 AU of Earth
Would trigger active planetary defense response

neo.body: Seven close approaches this week (Aug 17–23, JPL CNEOS) — none inside one lunar distance; the nearest, 2026 PX, passes at ~2.4 LD on August 23. Nothing on the Sentry risk list carries a Torino rating above zero. The catalog stands near 39,000 known NEOs, and growth means safety: every object found is one that can't surprise us. DART already proved deflection works.
neo.method: NASA CNEOS close approach database. Close approach = within 0.05 AU (~7.5M km). Impact probability from JPL Sentry automated orbital mechanics. Potentially hazardous: >140m + intersects within 0.05 AU. Updated daily from automated telescope observations worldwide.
neo.share: 7 NEO close approaches this week — all safe, none inside 1 lunar distance. ~39,000 known, 0 threats. anthonycharts.com ☄️

gini.title: Wealth Inequality

trend.label: Widening — COVID accelerated gap, no recovery

gini.body: The World Inequality Report 2026 puts the top 1% at 37% of global wealth — 18 times everything the bottom half owns combined; the top 10% hold about 75%, the bottom 50% share 2%. UBS's 2026 Global Wealth Report, using a different method, puts the top-1% share at 47.5%. Whichever lens, the direction is unchanged: the COVID-era widening has not reversed. A precision note: the headline 0.67 is an income-style Gini from the WID series — wealth Ginis run far higher (~0.88).
gini.method: Global Gini from World Inequality Database (WID.world) — maintained by Piketty, Chancel, Saez, and Zucman. Gini: 0 = perfect equality, 1 = perfect inequality. Arc normalized against 0–1.0 scale, with 0.8 as practical ceiling. Updated annually with World Inequality Report.
gini.share: Top 1% own 37% of global wealth — 18x the entire bottom half combined (World Inequality Report 2026). anthonycharts.com ⚖️

mobility.title: Social Mobility Index

trend.label: Stalled — no meaningful global progress since 2020

levels.label: Below average — South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa

mobility.body: The Global Social Mobility Index scores countries 0–100 across 10 pillars; the global average of 53.4 reflects a world where birthplace still largely determines outcomes. An attribution correction this issue: this is the World Economic Forum's 2020 index — it has not been re-published since, and no World Bank global 0–100 score exists. The freshest related data, a 2025 World Bank database of intergenerational income mobility across 87 countries, confirms the pattern: mobility rises with national income, and global progress has stalled since 2020. The metric is carried as stale-but-labeled until a real successor exists.
mobility.method: WEF Global Social Mobility Index (2020, unrevised): 10 equal-weight pillars — health, education access, education quality, lifelong learning, technology access, work opportunities, fair wages, working conditions, social protection, institutions. Supplemented by Opportunity Insights intergenerational income mobility data and the World Bank's 2025 income-mobility database. No update since 2020 — carried as stale-but-labeled.
mobility.share: Social Mobility: 53.4/100 globally — unchanged since the WEF's 2020 index, because no one has re-measured it. Where you're born still decides too much. anthonycharts.com 📈

conflict.title: Conflict Deaths

trend.label: Corrected — re-anchored to ACLED's published Conflict Index

stats.lbl: RU Claimed Losses · Jul · incl. wounded

rows.note: 6.1 correction — re-anchored to ACLED Conflict Index

levels.label: Current pace — elevated above pre-2022 avg
Very High — major interstate war level

conflict.body: A correction, on the record: the 28,400 battle-deaths-YTD figure this tile carried since launch could not be traced to any ACLED publication, and it is inconsistent with ACLED's own published scale — the ACLED Conflict Index recorded ~244,700 fatalities from political violence worldwide in the 12 months through November 2025, roughly 20,000 per month, which would put a genuine year-to-date count near 150,000 by mid-August, not 28,400. The tile is now anchored to ACLED's published Conflict Index figure and will update when ACLED publishes its next annual index. A definitional note prompted this check: headlines of "45,000 Russian soldiers lost this past month" trace to Ukraine's General Staff July figure of 42,860 — which counts killed, wounded, missing, and captured; independent death-only estimates (Mediazona/BBC confirmed records, probate-registry analysis) run at roughly one-third of claimed losses. Claimed casualties, verified deaths, and coded fatalities are three different measures — this dashboard now says which one it uses. The World On Edge DEATHS input (15%) is being re-based against the corrected scale for issue 7.
conflict.method: ACLED Conflict Index — fatalities coded from reported political-violence events across all conflicts worldwide; conservative by design, and deliberately undercounts military deaths ACLED deems unverifiable (notably Ukraine). Cross-referenced with UCDP. Correction Aug 2026 (issue 6.1): the prior 28,400 YTD figure was retired after failing a source check; the tile now carries ACLED's published 12-month Conflict Index figure. Battle-death-only YTD reporting resumes if/when ACLED publishes one.
conflict.share: Corrected: conflict fatalities re-anchored to ACLED's published Conflict Index — ~245K worldwide in the 12 months through Nov 2025. The old 28.4K YTD figure failed its source check and is retired. anthonycharts.com 💔

peace.title: Peacekeeping Reach

trend.label: Corrected — official UN count: 59,376 across 11 missions

rows.note: Corrected to official UN fact sheet · 11 missions

peace.body: A correction, not just an update: this dashboard previously carried 87,000 personnel across 12 missions, which does not match official UN reporting. The UN's own fact sheet lists 59,376 total personnel — 50,963 troops, 5,852 police, plus observers and staff — across 11 peacekeeping operations, drawn from 121 contributing countries. That is roughly half the 2015 peak of 120,000. The correction steepens the story this tile has always told: the world's response capacity is shrinking while its conflict map grows.
peace.method: UN peacekeeping fact sheets (peacekeeping.un.org). Personnel = troops + police + military observers + staff officers + civilians. Mission count = active mandated operations. Prior 87K/12 figure corrected Aug 2026 to the official series. Updated from UN reporting.
peace.share: Corrected: 59,376 UN peacekeepers across 11 missions — half the 2015 peak, per the UN's own fact sheet. 30+ countries in conflict vs 11 missions. anthonycharts.com 🕊️

species.title: Species Threat Index

trend.label: Rising — threat rate accelerating, 902 confirmed extinct since 1500

levels.label: Elevated crisis — mass extinction indicators active

species.body: The July 2026 Red List update (2026-1) lists 49,505 species as threatened — 28.1% of 175,909 assessed, both new highs as assessment coverage grows. Fifteen more species were declared Extinct, including six mammals. More than half of assessed hydrothermal-vent molluscs are threatened by prospective deep-sea mining — a frontier extinction risk arriving before the industry does. One recovery: the numbat improved. The share at risk holds near 28%: the rising count partly reflects wider assessment; the composition reflects real pressure.
species.method: IUCN Red List — the world's most comprehensive biodiversity database. Assessed across nine categories from Least Concern to Extinct. Threatened = Vulnerable + Endangered + Critically Endangered. Updated quarterly. Arc = threatened % of assessed, normalized against 50% ceiling.
species.share: 49,505 species now threatened — 28% of all assessed. 15 more declared extinct in the July Red List update. anthonycharts.com 🦏

conserve.title: Conservation Coverage

trend.label: Growing — but below pace required for 30x30 by 2030

conserve.body: 17.6% of land and 8.2% of oceans are formally protected — up from 14% land and 3% ocean in 2010. The 30x30 target was agreed at COP15 in Montreal i...
conserve.method: Protected Planet database by UNEP-WCMC and IUCN. Counts nationally designated protected areas and OECMs (Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures). Updated annually with country submissions to the Convention on Biological Diversity. Arc = % of 30x30 land target achieved.
conserve.share: 17.6% land protected. 8.2% ocean. Racing toward 30x30 by 2030 — ocean will fall short at current pace. Paired with Species Threat. anthonycharts.com 🌿

supply.title: Global Trade Stress

trend.label: Holding high — Hormuz shut; PMI input corrected

levels.label: High stress — visible supply chain disruption
Current (81) — crisis-level, easing from the 88 peak

supply.body: Trade Stress edges up to 82/100. The Strait of Hormuz has effectively closed — zero transits on August 16 against a pre-war ~178/day, war-risk premiums at 3–10% of hull value — and transpacific container rates hit new highs (Asia–US East Coast at $9,400/FEU), with the Drewry composite roughly 80% above a year ago. One correction pulls the other way: this composite previously carried a manufacturing PMI of 47.2 (contraction), but the published J.P.Morgan global PMI was 52.2 in June and 51.1 in July — decelerating expansion, not contraction. The corrected input is applied this issue and keeps the composite below its 88–95 wartime peaks even as shipping stress worsens.
supply.method: Experimental composite: Freightos Baltic Index (35%) — global container freight benchmark normalized historically. Manufacturing PMI inverted (35%) — S&P Global composite, inverted so contraction = higher stress. World Bank trade volume momentum (30%) — month-over-month change. Weights at anthonycharts.com/composites-v1.0.json
supply.share: Trade Stress: 82/100. Hormuz effectively shut, transpacific freight at record highs (+80% YoY). PMI input corrected: 51.1 — expansion, not contraction. anthonycharts.com 🚢

truth.title: Information Integrity Index

trend.label: Declining — every published input pointing down

levels.label: High integrity — most major claims accurate
Low — majority of claims unverified or false

truth.body: Information Integrity slips to 48.6%. Every measurable input worsened this cycle. RSF's 2026 index puts press freedom at a 25-year low, with over half of countries in 'difficult' or 'very serious' conditions for the first time. NewsGuard's monitor finds top AI chatbots repeating false claims 35% of the time (versus 18% a year ago) and counts 3,749 AI content-farm sites, up from 3,006 in March. IFCN reports 76% of fact-checking organizations in financial crisis after funding withdrawals. There is now a dedicated false-claims tracking center solely for the Iran war.
truth.method: Experimental composite: IFCN claim accuracy rate (50%) — from IFCN-verified fact-checkers internationally. RSF Press Freedom Index inverted (30%) — higher freedom = higher integrity score. NewsGuard credibility average (20%) — ratings of major news and information sources. Experimental — weights subject to revision, published at anthonycharts.com/composites-v1.0.json
truth.share: Information Integrity: 48.6%. Press freedom at a 25-year low, AI chatbots repeating false claims 35% of the time, 3,749 AI content farms and counting. anthonycharts.com 🎯
